{"level": 0, "why": "I am selecting the lowest/no-assessment option because the bundle does not contain the record the question is built on. If level 0 is instead meant to denote active value destruction, that reading is NOT supported by this bundle — the correct output in that case is the INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE statements below, not a substantive grade.

=== WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE BUNDLE (facts first, so you can disagree) ===

F1 FACT [10-Q Q3FY25, acc. 0000723125-25-000021, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]: "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102" (nine months ended May 29, 2025 vs May 30, 2024).
F2 FACT [same, investing]: "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)".
F3 FACT [same]: "Proceeds from government incentives | 1,294 | 267".
F4 FACT [same, financing]: "Payments of dividends to shareholders | (392) | (384)".
F5 FACT [same]: "Repayments of debt | (3,604) | (1,816)".
F6 FACT [MD&A, Financing Activities]: "net cash provided by financing activities consisted primarily of $1.68 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2029 Term Loan A; approximately $1.25 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2035 B Notes; approximately $1.00 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2035 A Notes; and $499 million of proceeds from the issuance of the 2032 Notes; partially offset by $3.60 billion of repayments of debt".
F7 FACT [same]: "Net increase (decrease) in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash | 3,117 | (992)".
F8 FACT [Note – Equity]: "No shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2025. Through May 29, 2025, we had repurchased an aggregate of $7.19 billion under the authorization."
F9 FACT [Item 2, Part II]: "During the quarter ended May 29, 2025, we did not repurchase any common stock under the authorization and as of May 29, 2025, $2.81 billion of the authorization remained available for the repurchase of our common stock."
F10 FACT [Risk Factors]: "Our expenditures for these share repurchases were $300 million in 2024, $425 million in 2023, $2.43 billion in 2022, $1.20 billion in 2021, $176 million in 2020, and $2.66 billion in 2019."
F11 FACT [Note – CHIPS Act Funding Agreements]: "Share repurchases are permitted during the first two years of such five-year period up to amounts specified in the funding agreements to help offset the dilutive effects of employee stock compensation or as otherwise permitted by the U.S. Department of Commerce."
F12 FACT [Note – Equity]: "We declared and paid dividends of $0.115 per share in the first, second, and third quarters of 2025."
F13 FACT [Note – Equity]: "On June 25, 2025, our Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.115 per share, payable in cash on July 22, 2025".
F14 FACT [Balance Sheet]: "Goodwill | 1,150 | 1,150" (May 29, 2025 vs August 29, 2024).
F15 FACT [Balance Sheet]: "Common stock, $0.10 par value, 3,000 shares authorized, 1,263 shares issued and 1,119 outstanding (1,253 shares issued and 1,109 outstanding as of August 29, 2024)".
F16 FACT [Balance Sheet]: "Treasury stock, 144 shares held (144 shares as of August 29, 2024)".
F17 FACT [Item 2, Part II, withholding table]: "March 28, 2025 | – | April 24, 2025 | 38,763 | 70.20 | —".
F18 FACT [Cash Flows]: "Stock-based compensation | 722 | 620".
F19 FACT [Note – Equity Compensation Plans]: "Restricted stock award shares granted | 11 | 12" and "Weighted-average grant-date fair value per share | $100.25 | $69.02".
F20 FACT [Statements of Operations]: "Operating income (loss) | 2,169 | 719 | 6,116 | (218)".
F21 FACT [Liquidity]: "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion."
F22 FACT [Liquidity]: "Construction of the fab began in October 2023, with first DRAM wafer output projected in the second half of calendar 2027."
F23 FACT [Liquidity]: "Cash and marketable investments totaled $12.21 billion as of May 29, 2025, and $9.15 billion as of August 29, 2024."
F24 FACT [Risk Factors]: "As of May 29, 2025, we had debt with a carrying value of $15.54 billion".
F25 FACT [Note – Debt]: "In the third quarter of 2025, we recognized a $46 million loss in other non-operating income (expense) on prepayment of the 2027 Notes."
F26 FACT [MD&A, Gross Margin]: "Improvements in our consolidated gross margins for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025 compared to corresponding periods of 2024 were primarily due to increases in average selling prices for DRAM products, manufacturing cost reductions, and an increased mix in sales of high-margin cloud products, particularly HBM."

=== WHAT FOLLOWS, AND WHERE IT STOPS ===

I1 INFERENCE (F2, F4, F8, F5/F6): Within the nine months covered, the deployment ranking by absolute dollars is reinvestment first ($10,199m capex), then gross debt repayment ($3,604m, largely refinanced by $4,430m of new issuance per F6), then dividends ($392m), then zero buyback and zero acquisition; cash balances rose (F7).
I2 INFERENCE (F14): No goodwill movement across the two balance-sheet dates, and no acquisition line appears in investing activities (F2/F3 exhaust the material items) — consistent with no acquisition and no goodwill impairment in the period.
I3 INFERENCE (F15, F16): Treasury shares are unchanged and both issued and outstanding share counts rose; the "Repurchase of stock – withholdings on employee equity awards" charges shown in the equity statement were tax withholdings, not retirement of shares against an authorization, and they did not offset issuance under equity plans. Share count rose over the nine months.
I4 INFERENCE (F8, F9, F11): The absence of buybacks in FY2025 to date is at least partly a constraint, not purely a discretionary price judgement, because the CHIPS funding agreements cap repurchases at dilution-offset levels for two years from December 9, 2024.
I5 INFERENCE (F20, F22, F26): The operating-income swing from $(218)m to $6,116m nine-month-over-nine-month is attributed by management to pricing, cost reduction and HBM mix, while the U.S. capex now being spent does not produce wafers until second half of calendar 2027 — so the current profit change cannot be read as the return on the current capex.

=== THE GAPS THAT MAKE THE QUESTION UNANSWERABLE ===

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (proportions, item 1)
  needed: capital deployment expressed as proportions of cash generated, period by period.
  why: the bundle gives absolute nine-month cash-flow lines for FY2025 and FY2024 only (F1–F7) and contains no <computed_metrics> block; rule 3 forbids me deriving the proportions.
  would_change: with a multi-period proportional series I could say whether reinvestment share is rising into a cyclical peak (a warning) or falling (a discipline signal).

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (buyback price discipline, starred item 2)
  needed: the pre-computed average repurchase price per period against that period's price range.
  why: the bundle gives dollar totals by fiscal year only (F10), with no share counts or average prices for those years, and zero repurchases in the period under review (F8, F9). The single average price present, $70.20 (F17), is tax-withholding on vesting, not an allocation decision.
  would_change: if repurchases had been made near period highs across several years, that is a policy-not-decision finding and caps the grade; if concentrated near period lows, it is evidence of genuine discipline.

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (acquisition scorecard, item 3)
  needed: consideration paid, goodwill recognised, and subsequent impairment over a long window.
  why: the bundle is one quarterly filing; goodwill is flat at $1,150m (F14) and no acquisition is disclosed. Nine months is too short a window for the impairment test the question asks for.
  would_change: a disclosed impairment of previously acquired assets would be direct evidence of value destroyed; a long clean window at constant goodwill would be weak positive evidence.

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (reinvestment quality, item 4)
  needed: the pre-computed series of incremental capital deployed against the subsequent change in operating profit.
  why: absent; I have two capex figures (F2) and two operating-income figures (F20) and am forbidden from turning them into an incremental return. Micron is also cyclical (F26), so a single pairing would be uninformative even if I were permitted to compute it.
  would_change: a multi-cycle series showing operating profit rising with cumulative capex would support a high grade; a series showing capex rising while trough profits do not would support a low one.

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (said versus did, starred item 6)
  needed: E-12, the list of management's stated capital-allocation commitments.
  why: no E-12 exhibit is in the bundle. The only testable forward statements I can see are inside the filing itself: the ~$14 billion FY2025 net capex estimate (F21) — not yet testable, since FY2025 is not complete as of the May 29, 2025 period end; the quarterly dividend (F12, F13) — kept for the three quarters shown; and the $10bn repurchase authorisation (F8, F9), which is explicitly non-binding and now constrained (F11), so "not kept" would be the wrong label and "not yet testable" the right one.
  would_change: if E-12 contained, say, a stated capital-return target or a capex ceiling, I could mark each commitment kept/not kept and grade the record.

ASSUMPTION: I have assumed that rubric level 0 is the "cannot be assessed from this evidence" option rather than a substantive worst-case grade. If that is wrong, treat the INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE blocks above as my answer and disregard the numeric selection.", "what_would_move_it_down": "Moving to the adjacent substantive option (level 1) requires only that E-07 supply a multi-period deployment-and-repurchase series and E-12 supply the commitment list — with those, the $10,199m of nine-month capex, the zero FY2025 repurchases under a still-open $10bn authorisation, and the rising share count (1,109 to 1,119 outstanding) become gradeable rather than merely descriptive."}
